title: Manuel Durón to W. Olliphant (González Garza), México to El Paso, 20 May 1911: warning against Licenciado Reyes Retana, read in part with a shift on a 29-sign alphabet (key not validated, text too short)

documents.shelfmark: CEHM-Carso, Fondo CMXV (Archivo Federico González Garza), CMXV.18.1777.1-6
documents.route: Manuel Durón (México) -> W. Olliphant = Federico González Garza (El Paso)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the sheet; not in the typed list of period decipherments CMXV.18.1795.1; catalogue 1462 lists it as undeciphered.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout, from the CEHM viewer image (study copy, not redistributed)
transcription.notes: Received telegram, 9:10 pm, no. 428; 23 groups, 115 letters = 107 signs with ll as one sign; 'YELL Y' spaced so on the form; the space in 'VJLLL LYJXY' falls inside 'll ll'.

system.summary: A simple shift on a 29-sign Spanish alphabet (a b c ch d e f g h i j k l ll m n ñ o p q r s t u v w x y z): cipher = plain + 22; two header signs; the cipher sign ñ is typed 'n' by the telegraph, so cipher n reads t or u. Recovered from the ciphertext; not validated (107 signs).

prior_solution.where: No gloss on the sheet; absent from the typed list of period decipherments CMXV.18.1795.1 (45 pp., OCR searched: on 20 May only Elisa 1777.2-6, Herrera Moreno x2 and Miranda/Herrera Moreno; no 'Retana' outside Elisa). Catalogue 1462 lists 18.1777.1-6 as undeciphered; nothing in the issues (#330, #351) or PRs. Narváez 2019 (SRE book, ch. VII-VIII) could not be checked.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. Claude (Opus) agents transcribed the telegram from the CEHM viewer image, froze the transcription and a protocol before decoding, ran the single archive-key measure, recovered the key by annealing and a shift sweep, and wrote this up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout (transcription, protocol and measure, key recovery, reading, write-up)

solution.what: Telegram transcribed from the CEHM viewer image and hashed (T-sanantonio-duron-v1.txt, 100db048...) before any key was tried; rechecked on the image on 12 Nov 2026, unchanged.
IC 0.076 with ll as one sign (107 signs, 18 letters, none of a b o p q s u z): a simple substitution, not a transposition (the turning grille of nuevaclave1911 keeps Spanish frequencies).

Preregistered single measure (PREREG-C06, frozen before decoding): every key of the fonds as is (the Elisa shift +-10 of 1777.2-6, the .tsv cards and tables of CMXV.16.1557.1 incl. the Clave G.A.); lexicon coverage W against 200 random substitutions. Best W 0.259 (Elisa +10) vs best control 0.365: no archive key applies (MESURE-C06.txt).
General substitution anneal on Spanish trigrams, no shift assumed: '...madero de licenciado... reyes retana y compañeros... correo detalles'; the table found is a shift.
Every shift on six alphabets (26, 27, 28, 28 without w, 27 with ch-ll, 29): only 29 signs / +22 reads (score -10.1 against at best -13.2 for any other).

Words counted by the README rule, header excluded: 19 words, 15 sure, 3 probable (Daniel, a, la), 1 unresolved (dak): strict 15/19 = 78.9 %, with probable words 18/19 = 94.7 %. 'danlel' has one wrong sign; the sister telegram 1777.2-6 names Ismael Reyes Retana, so the first name is doubtful.

No validation possible: 107 signs, under the 300 letters a held-out measure needs; declared in PREREG-C06 before decoding. Observed after the reading and not counted: shift = header sign 1 - header sign 2, as in the sister telegram 1777.2-6 (P - H = +10 on 28 signs).

validation.notes: Declared in advance (PREREG-C06, frozen before decoding): 107 signs, no held-out portion of 300 letters possible, so no reading can be validated and the best status is 'read in part'. The key was built on the whole text. The single preregistered measure only tested the archive's keys (none applies). Contributor's own protocol, not docs/_validate.py.

outcome.method_basis: The key was recovered from the ciphertext alone: a free substitution anneal and an exhaustive sweep of shifts on six alphabets give the same table, a shift of +22 on 29 signs. Not validated: the text is too short (declared in advance). The reading rests on the sense of the Spanish (names, one sentence per clause) and on the sister telegram 1777.2-6, which reports a Reyes Retana plot the same day.

outcome.notes: One telegram of 20 May 1911 (eve of the Treaty of Ciudad Juárez), read in part with a key recovered from the ciphertext. Key not validated (107 signs; declared in advance). Strict count 15 of 19 words = 78.9 %; with the 3 probable words 94.7 %. A different key from the Clave G.A. (mccarty1911), the turning grille (nuevaclave1911), the Hernández card (hernandez1911), the signer's card of mexico1911 and the Elisa shift (1777.2-6).
outcome.fraction_read_source: dudout/reading.md, by words (README rule), header excluded: 19 words, 15 sure = 78.9 %; 3 probable (Daniel, a, la) and 1 unresolved (dak) not counted as read. Counting the probable words: 18 of 19 = 94.7 %.

texts.label: Manuel Durón, México, to W. Olliphant, El Paso, 20 May 1911 (CEHM-Carso CMXV.18.1777.1-6)
texts.summary: Mexico City, evening of 20 May 1911: Madero must beware of Licenciado {Daniel} Reyes Retana and companions, who have left for El Paso; let me know; details by mail. The sister telegram of that afternoon (1777.2-6) reports Ismael Reyes Retana as head of a plot to kill Madero. Key not validated.

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences against the translation: four short clauses, no hole except 'dak'; the first name is doubtful (one wrong sign; Ismael in the sister telegram). Key not validated (text too short). Strict count 15 of 19 words = 78.9 %.
